title: Three Winters and One Short Ridge
subtitle: 森林生态 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 森林生态（人与自然·自然生态·森林与生态）
meta: 主题语境：森林生态（人与自然·自然生态·森林与生态）　|　核心词汇：forest　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 forest 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the guide ① crossed a forest that no keeper in the region would have mapped, and he said the crossing was the whole of the winter. The ② forest, meaning the woods itself and not the tree, ran three winters and stayed unmapped in the book; a forest, he said, is the only thing in a region that is judged by how long it is left unmapped.

Every ③ forest in that region had the same short ridge beside it, and the ④ forest at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A forest, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to map; the guide said the mapping is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the forest was the whole of the matter, meaning the crowd and not the woods. The ⑥ forest, meaning the crowd and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody maps; forest, he said, is either something you cross or the only word that means both woods and a crowd. He said the crowd is the part they remember.

By 1973 the ⑦ forest had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short ridge. The ⑧ forest of the whole thing, the guide wrote in January, was one region and three winters of mapping; forest, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to map. He said the mapping was never mentioned.

The ⑨ forest I remember is the one mapped in the plan, which closed in 1975 and is still described as the quietest in the region. A ⑩ forest, my mother said in 1977, is the only one that improves by being mapped; every forest, she said, is a crowd that has agreed to look like woods. She said the crowd was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 森林；林区（指这一带每一片旁边的那一片）
B. n. 森林（指那一片本身，与单株树木相对）
C. 固定搭配：cross a forest 穿过一片森林
D. n. 森林（指留给孩子们的那一片）
E. n. 森林（抽象总称，指一个地区的林区之事）
F. n. 森林（指计划里写到、被测绘过的那一片）
G. n. 林立；一片（a forest of masts，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 林立（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: crossed a forest that no keeper in the region would have mapped
The forest, meaning the woods itself and not the tree
the forest at the far end
the forest was the whole of the matter
the forest had become a line in a plan
The forest of the whole thing
A forest, my mother said in 1977

answers.why: cross a forest 意为“穿过一片森林”，1966 年那位向导穿过了一片这一带没有一位看守人肯测绘的森林。
forest 意为“森林”，指那一片本身而不是单株树木，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被测绘。
forest 意为“森林”，指这一带每一片旁边的那一片，每一片旁边都有同一道矮矮的山脊。
forest 意为“森林”，指留给孩子们的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
forest 意为“林立、一片”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这一片林立就是那件事的全部。
forest 意为“林立”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那一片森林，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
forest 意为“森林”，指计划里写到、被测绘过的那一片，到 1973 年这一片成了计划里的一行。
forest 意为“森林”，向导一月写道，整件事的林区之事是一个地区和三个冬天的测绘。
forest 意为“森林”，我记得的是计划里测绘过的那一片，1975 年结束了，至今仍被说成这一带最安静的一片。
forest 为抽象总称，母亲 1977 年说，一片森林是唯一会因为被好好测绘而变得更好的东西。
